programs.nl_rule:
In the input, you should see...colored rectangular shapes on a black background

The output grid size...is the same as the input grid size

To make the output, you have to...replace all colored blocks inside the rectangular shapes with black so there is only a colored outline of the shapes

content.text:
Let me understand the rule. Input has colored rectangular shapes on black background. Output: replace interior of colored blocks with black, leaving only outline. So hollow out each object: set all cells except those in the box outline to background color.

Let me create a demonstration. Show example with a simple rectangle, maybe two rectangles of different colors.

Let me make a demonstration that's not a near-copy of the teacher example. Let me use a different shape/size and maybe multiple colors.

Let me author an input and output that match the rule.

Example: 7x7 grid with a 3x3 red square and a 2x4 blue rectangle.

Actually let me just compute carefully.

Input 8x8:
Row0: all 0
Row1: 0 3 3 3 0 0 0 0
Row2: 0 3 3 3 0 0 0 0
Row3: 0 3 3 3 0 0 0 0
Row4: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row5: 0 0 0 0 0 4 4 0
Row6: 0 0 0 0 0 4 4 0
Row7: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0

Output: hollow them.
3x3 square rows1-3, cols1-3: outline = corners and edges; interior is (2,2). So keep all except (2,2) becomes 0.
2x2 square rows5-6 cols5-6: no interior, stays same.

Output:
Row0: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row1: 0 3 3 3 0 0 0 0
Row2: 0 3 0 3 0 0 0 0
Row3: 0 3 3 3 0 0 0 0
Row4: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row5: 0 0 0 0 0 4 4 0
Row6: 0 0 0 0 0 4 4 0
Row7: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0

Good. Let me show that as example. Then maybe probe, then show another, then query, then exam.

Let me do show_example first.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

content.text:
Now probe with a fresh, unseen input. Let me make a 10x10 with a big rectangle 4x5.

Input 10x10:
Row0-9 all 0
Rectangle rows1-4 (4 rows), cols2-5 (4 cols) color 6.

Actually let's do rows1-5 (5 rows), cols1-4 (4 cols) color 7. Interior = rows2-4, cols2-3. Hollow them.

Grid 8x8:
Row0: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row1: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row2: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row3: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row4: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row5: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row6: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row7: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0

Interior rows2-4, cols2-3 -> 0.

Output:
Row0: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row1: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row2: 0 7 0 0 7 0 0 0
Row3: 0 7 0 0 7 0 0 0
Row4: 0 7 0 0 7 0 0 0
Row5: 0 7 7 7 7 0 0 0
Row6: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
Row7: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0

Let me query student with this input.

content.text:
Student correct on unseen input. Wait, but note the query input was unseen and correct. Start exam.

Actually the check: "start_exam is held until your most recent query_student, made after your last demonstration on an input the student has not seen, came back correct". Yes, satisfied. Start exam.
